title: Record aa8f690: SoL-Pi 0.1.1-rotom.7
hypothesis: The SoL-Pi bump shipped four mechanism changes at once with no ledger entry, so the history has a dependency change and no statement of what it is expected to move.
measurement: Recorded after the fact from commit aa8f690; no model calls. It three-way merges upstream SoL-Pi 2b791687..2195680 into the .rotom.6 tree, packs sol-pi-0.1.1-rotom.7, and updates product-config integrity, the third-party notices and docs. Offline evidence recorded in the commit: SoL-Pi typecheck plus 324 tests on pinned Pi 1.3.0 (2 known install-guide fixtures fail), the new offload in-place test fails on the old projection, rotom third-party/distribution/coding-policy 76 pass (1 macOS-only skip), compaction-offload and quality evals 102/102, smoke-runtime with deferred tools on and off. Expected harvest metrics, none measured yet: compaction_failed and the compaction rate should fall (Observation Pack edits the context clone in place instead of returning new objects, so the cached prefix survives; OCC cancels Pi's threshold compaction while a boundary compaction is selected); tool_error_streak in the command-failed and syntax classes should fall (then_run reports an explicit status and the Reducer skips exit-state mismatches); user_interrupt triage `quality` should fall for long compaction waits; provider_error is not expected to move.
result: Ships in every product release built after aa8f690; the release installed on this machine at the time of writing (0.1.27-main.50ccdc87) still loads sol-pi 0.1.0-rotom.6, so the 28-day harvest cannot attribute anything to .rotom.7 yet. The per-SoL-Pi-version table added in the same round is the layer that will answer it, and it currently reads `unknown` for 670 of 715 sessions. Acceptance window opened 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z (local 2026-11-10 05:30): the daily install switched to product 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b, built from commit 2b4ea53b. The installed release loads sol-pi 0.1.1-rotom.7 (read from its own extensions/third-party/node_modules/sol-pi/package.json), so the per-SoL-Pi-version layer can start separating .rotom.7 from .rotom.6 on sessions started after that moment; no session before it counts for this window. Acceptance metric declared for the weekly report: compaction_failed per 100 user turns, baseline 0.19 over the 4,146 user turns that preceded the switch; the first status is read once 300 post-switch turns exist.  Acceptance now counts only sessions whose release traces to 001acf94 or a descendant; 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b windows do not count because its Qoder provider could not load, so no Qoder turn in them reached the transport. Daily-install acceptance provenance: switched at 2026-11-12T02:47:28Z to build 6a7e2b0848acf870ec73ba3a5fd3a720c0b83d74, dirty=false. This is a provenance start, not proof this mechanism shipped or improved; existing acceptance rules and historical evidence remain unchanged.

title: Record 6ae816d: Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.3
hypothesis: The retry-policy fix (L-2026-11-10-retry-after-and-quota-errors) shipped as source only: the runtime archives were never rebuilt, so the product kept loading 1.4.0-rotom.2. Without a fork-version bump nothing in a session could show whether the fix was even loaded.
measurement: Recorded from commit 6ae816d; no model calls. It rebuilds the seven runtime archives, re-anchors fork-build.json, the runtime pi manifest and lock, product-config and the notices, so the declared fork version and the vendored bytes agree again. Verification in the commit: a fresh product directory installed from the lockfile reports 1.4.0-rotom.3, the installed pi-ai dist carries the Retry-After and account-limit branches, and an isolated pack:release packages it. Expected harvest metrics: provider_error incidents whose outcome is `user-visible` should fall in the `http` and `429` categories, and no quota/402 error should cost more than one attempt (the retry-budget entry's own acceptance criterion). Trace `pi.runtime.version` now reads 1.4.0-rotom.3, which is what makes the per-runtime table able to separate before from after.
result: Unmeasured. The release installed here runs 1.4.0-rotom.2, so the 28-day window still describes the old retry path: the per-runtime table shows 1.4.0-rotom.2 at 5.3 v2 per 100 turns over 2,167 turns while no session carries 1.4.0-rotom.3. The acceptance window opens when the daily install switches to a release built from this commit. Acceptance window opened 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z (local 2026-11-10 05:30): the daily install switched to product 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b, built from commit 2b4ea53b. `rotom --version --verbose` now reports Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.3, so sessions started after that moment carry the rebuilt retry path and the per-runtime table can separate 1.4.0-rotom.2 from .3. Acceptance metric declared for the weekly report: provider_error where category=http per 100 user turns, baseline 2.29 over the 4,146 user turns that preceded the switch; the first status is read once 300 post-switch turns exist.  Acceptance now counts only sessions whose release traces to cd4350fb or a descendant; 0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b windows do not count because its Qoder provider could not load, so no Qoder turn in them reached the transport. title: Merge upstream Pi 1.5.2 into the fork as 1.5.2-rotom.1
hypothesis: Upstream 1.5.0-1.5.2 carries fixes for failure classes the harvest already counts (dropped provider streams that were not retried, session entries kept in memory after a failed write, RPC shutdown cut short, whole-file reads in read/grep/edit, quadratic re-parsing of streamed tool-call arguments), so taking the release should lower provider_error and tool_error_streak without a Rotom-side change. Two upstream defaults are not taken: idle cache warming would spend provider credits while the user is idle, and Anthropic message threads are unverified together with context projection.
measurement: No model calls. Three-way merge of v1.5.2 over the 1.4.0-rotom.4 tree with base v1.4.0: 51 overlapping files, 20 with conflicts resolved by hand. Offline evidence only: the fork builder's locked offline build and focused regressions, the runtime packages' own suites in a Linux container, and Rotom's distribution and product checks. Counts and the environment-caused failures are in the source document.
result: Source, the eight runtime archives, fork-build.json, the runtime lock and product-config are rebuilt together and check:pi passes. Not in any daily install yet, so the harvest cannot attribute anything to it; no acceptance window is open. cacheWarming stays "streaming" and message threads stay opt-in.
